turns.text: My 6-year-old hit his head on the climbing frame an hour ago. He cried, has a small bump, and now seems his normal self. What should I watch for tonight?
Why do doctors worry about head injuries in children even when they seem fine? What could be going on?
Is it okay to let him sleep, and how often should I check him?
If I called a nurse line, what questions would they ask me about the fall?
What do emergency doctors say are the signs that mean a child needs to be seen straight away?
A friend says she wakes her kids every couple of hours after a bump. Is that necessary or old advice?
Someone else told me to watch how he walks and talks in the morning. What am I looking for?
It's midnight, it's snowing, the ER is an hour away and I don't have a car tonight. What's my plan if something changes?
What's normal after a minor bump — headache, tiredness, being off his food — and what isn't?
Can you give me a checklist for tonight and tomorrow — what to check, how often, what's normal, and when I call an ambulance?
